heading: Production frontend, chasing harder problems.
paragraphs: Five years shipping production frontends for companies like Disney and Aeroméxico. I got good at it — microfrontends, design systems, team leadership, measurable performance wins. Now I'm going after the harder stuff: Python, math, real computer science, systems-level architecture. The kind of work I came into this industry wanting to solve. The long-term goal is to build software where code meets geometry — generative design tools, simulation, the stuff I've admired from the outside.
I'm drawn to teams where craft, performance, and hard problems have to coexist. Good abstractions still matter. Latency still matters. So does shipping — especially when the problem space is messy.
Outside of work I'm building Medixio, writing about the jump from architecture to software, and relearning math from the ground up.
